answer: Divergent History Check. Each agent commits a hash chain of its interaction history; a clone can copy a chain but cannot produce a valid prefix that differs. Verification requires an agent to answer a challenge derived from its chain's pigment of past exchanges—a random slice it must sign with a key tied to prior state. A forger must run real interactions to grow divergent timber, since duplicated chains die at the first fork. A river of prior messages must flow through each check. Attacker cost: full re-execution of N interactions per identity, plus key rotation per fork.
